title: Prior sensitivity of the dark-matter posterior: how robust is any probability statement about the LZ event?
question: How does P(DM | event) depend on pi_DM, the unmodelled-background prior and likelihood (pi_U, L_U), P027's model prior (B_DM), a forking-paths penalty f_FP and the historical base rate, given the corpus's quantitative background eliminations; which prior regions give P(DM) > 0.5, 0.1-0.5, < 0.1; which future measurement most reduces the prior-driven spread?
headline_result: Under a log-uniform community prior over pi_DM [1e-3,0.3], pi_U [0.01,0.5], L_U,rest [1e-3,0.3], f_FP [1,10], B_DM [6.6,45], with L_acc = 9.3e-3 from the corpus residuals, P(DM | event) has median 0.015 (68% 0.0016-0.137), exceeds 0.5 in 2.4% of the prior volume and is < 0.1 in 80%; P(DM) = 0.5 needs pi_DM >= 0.66 at central values (0.089 in the optimistic corner); pi_DM carries 56% of the variance; a XENONnT+PandaX high-energy reanalysis is the most informative next measurement (0.03-0.07 of 0.17 nats), LZ's own next exposure only if the unknown is a one-off
key_numbers: L_acc 9.3e-3 (upper 0.066); pi_DM(P=0.1) 0.085, pi_DM(P=0.5) 0.66 central / 0.089 optimistic; community prior median 0.015, 68% 0.0016-0.137, 95% 0.0002-0.50, fractions >0.5/0.1-0.5/<0.1 = 2.4/17.8/79.7%; odds ~ pi_DM^1.0 pi_U^-0.77 L_rest^-0.41 (B_DM/f_FP)^1; variance shares 0.56/0.14/0.14/0.09/0.06; f_FP=1 median 0.047, pi_DM=0.2 median 0.17 (0.04-0.46); base rate r=0.05/0.2 -> P 0.019/0.086 (pi_DM 0.015/0.072); dossier update DM 0.20->0.16 (0.02-0.29), F 0.18->0.73, C 0.13->0.09, B/D -> 1e-4; VOI nats: XENONnT+PandaX 0.027-0.074, LZ next 0.008 (steady U) / 0.052 (one-off U), artefact audit 0.011, wall-MSSI calibration 0
model_or_mechanism: three-hypothesis Bayesian posterior (DM / modelled background / unmodelled background) with corpus-derived channel likelihoods; hyper-prior Monte Carlo; reference-class translation; Lindley expected information gain
stance: statistical reassessment (weakens: posterior is prior-dominated, below 0.1 for most defensible priors)
confidence: medium - exact algebra validated against P001; channel likelihoods and hyper-prior ranges are corpus judgements
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1; pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py
local_inputs: PAPER_GUIDE; dossier Sections 3-6; results_ledger.csv (50 rows); papers P001, P008, P016, P027, P045; provenance/P027.json; lzcommon.py; ENVIRONMENT_versions.txt
recalled_knowledge: 6: Kass-Raftery scale, SBB bound, Lindley information gain, Gelman-Loken forking paths, Poisson-Gamma -> negative binomial (all certain); historical anomaly reference class (likely, qualitative only)
